2609.22959.title: R-GEAN: Regimen-Guided Edit Action Network for Within-Admission Medication Change Prediction
2609.22959.paper_summary: The medications prescribed to a patient often change during a hospital admission as clinicians start, stop, or continue therapies. We study whether models can predict which medication classes are added or removed between 24 hours after admission and discharge. Metrics that compare the complete discharge regimen can reward models for copying medications that remain unchanged, even when they identify no actual changes. We therefore introduce a leakage-controlled benchmark that predicts net ATC3 additions and removals using only prior completed admissions and information available within the first 24 hours of the current admission. Addition candidates are classes not active at 24 hours, whereas removal candidates are classes active at that time. We also introduce R-GEAN, an asymmetric candidate-scoring network with independent addition and removal predictors. Across 240,480 admissions from 82,286 patients, R-GEAN achieves the highest predefined summary of addition, removal, changed-regimen, and action-pattern performance, termed the edit composite (0.464), compared with 0.435 for the strongest primary comparator. Reimplemented RETAIN, GAMENet, and MICRON baselines obtain 0.428, 0.420, and 0.288, respectively. R-GEAN's advantage is concentrated in correctly identifying medication classes no longer active at discharge, while rare additions and admissions with multiple medication changes remain difficult. Rankings based on micro-F1 over the reconstructed discharge regimen and the edit composite correlate weakly across the evaluated models (Spearman r = 0.20). The continuation baseline achieves the highest complete-regimen score despite predicting no additions or removals. These results show that complete-regimen and edit-level evaluation measure different aspects of medication prediction. The benchmark evaluates observed prescribing changes, not treatment appropriateness
2609.22959.paper_summary_zh: 患者在住院期間所開立的藥物常常會變化，因為臨床醫生會開始、停止或繼續治療。<lb/>我們研究模型是否能預測在入院後24小時和出院之間，哪些藥物類別會被添加或移除。<lb/>比較完整出院方案的指標可能會因為複製未變更的藥物而獎勵模型，即使它們未識別出任何實際變化。<lb/>因此，我們引入了一個控制洩漏的基準，僅使用先前完成的住院資料和當前住院的前24小時內可用的資訊來預測淨ATC3的添加和移除。<lb/>添加候選類別是指在24小時內未活躍的類別，而移除候選類別則是指在該時間內活躍的類別。<lb/>我們還引入了R-GEAN，一個具有獨立添加和移除預測器的非對稱候選評分網絡。<lb/>在82,286名患者的240,480次住院中，R-GEAN在預定義的添加、移除、變更方案和行動模式表現總結中達到了最高的表現，稱為編輯綜合得分（0.464），而最強的主要比較者為0.435。<lb/>重新實現的RETAIN、GAMENet和MICRON基準分別獲得0.428、0.420和0.288。<lb/>R-GEAN的優勢集中在正確識別出院時不再活躍的藥物類別，而稀有的添加和多藥物變更的住院仍然困難。<lb/>基於重建的出院方案和編輯綜合得分的微F1排名在評估的模型之間相關性較弱（Spearman r = 0.20）。<lb/>儘管預測沒有添加或移除，持續基準仍然達到了最高的完整方案得分。<lb/>這些結果顯示，完整方案和編輯級別的評估衡量藥物預測的不同方面。<lb/>該基準評估觀察到的處方變化，而非治療的適當性。
